title: Power (Recursion)
directAnswer: Base case `n == 0` returns 1. Linear: `x * power(x, n-1)`. Fast: square `power(x, n/2)` and multiply by x if n is odd → O(log n).

remember.takeaway: Squaring the half-power gives O(log n) exponentiation.

problemStatement: Given a base `x` and non-negative integer exponent `n`, compute `xⁿ` recursively.
understanding: xⁿ = x · xⁿ⁻¹ (linear), or use fast exponentiation: xⁿ = (xⁿ/²)² for O(log n).

approaches.name: Fast exponentiation
approaches.whenToMention: This is the standard, expected solution — lead with it.
approaches.explanation:
Compute xⁿ recursively. The naive form xⁿ = x · xⁿ⁻¹ is O(n); the smart form is **exponentiation by squaring**: xⁿ = (x^(n/2))², times an extra x when n is odd — O(log n).

**Why squaring is O(log n).** Each call halves the exponent (`n/2`), so the recursion depth is log₂(n). For n = 10⁶ that's ~20 multiplications instead of a million.

**Compute the half-power ONCE.** The critical detail: store `half = power(x, n/2)` in a variable and use `half*half`. Writing `power(x,n/2)*power(x,n/2)` makes two recursive calls and destroys the speedup, collapsing back to O(n).

**The odd correction.** When n is odd, n/2 (integer) loses the half-step, so multiply the squared result by an extra x. Base case x⁰ = 1. This squaring trick is the engine behind modular exponentiation in crypto/hashing.
hints: x^n = x · x^(n-1) is O(n) — can halving the exponent help?
x^n = (x^(n/2))²; compute the half-power only ONCE.
Add a ×x correction when n is odd; base case x⁰ = 1.
approaches.insight: Knowing the O(log n) squaring trick — not just the linear recurrence — is the differentiator here.
approaches.complexityReasoning: halving the exponent each call gives log₂(n) depth with O(1) work per call.

java.explanation: Square it; multiply by x for odd exponents.

pitfalls: Calling power(x, n/2) twice (loses the O(log n) gain).

commonMistakes: Calling power(x, n/2) twice (loses the O(log n) gain).
patternNote: A core fresher pattern: Exponentiation by squaring. Master it on small inputs and it transfers to harder problems.

clarifyingQuestions.question: Non-negative exponent?
clarifyingQuestions.answer: Assuming n ≥ 0; negative n means 1/xⁿ as a double.

commonMistakesDetailed.title: Recomputing the half-power
commonMistakesDetailed.why: power(x,n/2)*power(x,n/2) makes two recursive calls, doubling work each level back to O(n).
commonMistakesDetailed.good: long h = power(x,n/2); return h*h;    // O(log n)
